clue.text: Apprehended a thug suspiciously joining in flashy techno dance

indicators.note: behaving suspiciously suggests the letters are moving about shiftily, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something flashy is showy and flamboyant, a second hint that these letters are jazzed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A thug behaving shiftily is arrested as he joins in a showy dance to techno music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspiciously' and 'flashy' both signal rearrangement: A THUG and TECHNO together are rearranged to make CAUGHT ON THE, then HOP is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken by surprise and seized in the act is a loose sense of being apprehended unawares.

clue.text: Mate briefly eating out wanting accompaniment for 8 or 13 Across?

indicators.note: one piece eating another takes it inside, so the shortened word surrounds the other
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or mate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pal, eating out, wants something to go with the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 and 13 Across are CONSOMME and POTAGE, both soups, which is why the definition is phrased as a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fried cubes of bread are the classic garnish floated on a clear or thick soup.

clue.text: Our Ben's terribly drunk

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words are badly mangled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that our friend Ben is awfully intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not sober is by plain logic intoxicated, the opposite of clear-headed.

clue.text: A politician's time in chief London district

indicators.note: in places the run of short pieces inside the word for chief

parts.note: a head is a chief or leader
an MP is a Member of Parliament; with the 's this gives MPS

explanation.surface: A politician spends time in the main part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampstead is a well-to-do area of north London famous for its Heath.

clue.text: Rambling review don had not completely finished

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A long-winded critique that a university don had not quite completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' belongs to the fodder; 'completely' looks like a modifier of it but sits in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means entirely finished with something, used of a task or relationship you have dealt with for good.

clue.text: Propose pill if not getting rest ultimately

indicators.note: not getting something means going without it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a tablet is a pill

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word rest

explanation.surface: A doctor proposes a pill for a patient who isn't sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: TABLET loses T, the last letter of 'rest'. In British usage to table a motion is to put it forward for discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: In British meetings, putting a motion forward for debate is to lay it on the table.

clue.text: Competitor in French race sprinted on the inside

parts.note: en is the French word for in

indicators.note: being on the inside puts one piece within the other

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
ran is a synonym of sprinted

explanation.surface: A rider in a French race sped along on the inside lane.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man's famous motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: One who enters a contest is a participant or rival in it.

clue.text: Turned up one over the eight during work: good start!

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: literally one more than eight is nine, though the phrase is slang for slightly drunk

explanation.surface: Someone turned up tipsy at work, a fine start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for a drink too many, but here it is just arithmetic: NINE, reversed by 'Turned up' to ENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is the beginning of something, as in the first move of a game.

clue.text: Dish soon polished off by males entering empty café

indicators.note: entering puts the middle letters inside the outer shell
an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters
polished off suggests the word is knocked about and reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male, so two males give MM

explanation.surface: A dish gobbled up quickly by men coming into a deserted café.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear meat or fish broth served as a course is a classic soup dish.

clue.text: Beer making you resentful

definitions.meaning: feeling aggrieved and sour about how one has been treated

explanation.surface: Drinking beer makes you sour.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names a hoppy pub ale and also describes a person full of grievance.

clue.text: Knife taken into constabulary

indicators.note: taken into means the letters are held within the word that follows

explanation.surface: A knife confiscated by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To knife someone is to wound them with a blade, a verb sense.

clue.text: 16 accommodation, say, sailor's occupying after start of cruise

indicators.note: after places the sailor and the following piece behind the first letter of cruise

parts.note: to state is to say

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor; the 's stands for is
being in a place is occupying it

explanation.surface: A sailor is in a ship's quarters once the cruise begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is ONBOARD, so the definition reads 'onboard accommodation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A private sleeping room on a ship is the passenger's lodging while at sea.

clue.text: Cease to be allied to peace keepers as day reaches close

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, provides peacekeeping forces
Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
an end is a close

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers withdraw support as the day comes to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing someone from your friends list on social media ends your online link with them.

clue.text: Reverse of, say, a first-class course

indicators.note: the reverse of a phrase reads its letters backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
top means first-class

explanation.surface: The opposite of a first-rate course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick soup served as the starter of a meal is one course of it.

clue.text: Fences fool put up to protect ladies in trouble

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the reversed word encloses the rearranged one
in a down entry, put up means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a sap is a fool

indicators.note: in trouble suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool erects fencing to shield women who are in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of stakes forming a defensive enclosure are a type of fencing.

clue.text: Men in Civil Defence backing current agreement

indicators.note: backing means supporting from behind, so the following piece sits after the current

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: in places the men inside the abbreviation for Civil Defence

parts.note: CD is the abbreviation for Civil Defence
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men

explanation.surface: Men of the Civil Defence support the present treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: An accord is a formal treaty or harmony between parties.

clue.text: Twin revolutionaries leading new republic

indicators.note: twin means two of the same, so the revolutionary appears twice

parts.note: Che Guevara was the famous Argentine revolutionary; twin Ches make the plural

explanation.surface: Two rebels are at the head of a newly formed state.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the word names the Chechen Republic in the Caucasus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chechen Republic is a federal state of Russia in the North Caucasus.

clue.text: Ready to join in, as directors are?

definitions.meaning: willing and committed to take part in a plan
company directors sit on the board

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means signed up to a scheme and also, literally, being a member of a board.

clue.text: One gazes at enthroned king and queen?

parts.note: the throne is jokey slang for a toilet, so enthroned is sitting on the loo
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone stares at the king and queen sitting on their thrones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthroned' is regal in the surface, but 'throne' is slang for a toilet: ON LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is someone who watches events without taking part.

clue.text: Extremists literally behind newspaper material

indicators.note: behind puts the extreme letters after the newspaper

parts.note: an organ is a publication speaking for a group
the letters at the extremes of the alphabet are Z and A

explanation.surface: Radicals stand behind a newspaper's material.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin, stiff, sheer fabric of silk or synthetic fibre.

clue.text: Mostly simple to oversee part of London

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: easy means simple
to tend is to look after or oversee

explanation.surface: It's fairly simple to manage a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditionally working-class area east of the City is a named district of the capital.

clue.text: Hears 5 will need preparing for drinks

indicators.note: preparing means making up, so the letters are made up afresh

parts.note: the answer to 5 Down is TABLE

explanation.surface: A note that something heard will need to be got ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Infusions of herbs in hot water are drinks taken instead of ordinary tea.

clue.text: One fever a type of drug initially eliminated

indicators.note: eliminated initially means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Class A is the UK legal category for the most harmful drugs

explanation.surface: A fever where a type of drug was first ruled out.
explanation.walkthrough: Class A is the most serious category of illegal drugs under UK law.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa fever is a viral haemorrhagic illness named after a town in Nigeria.

clue.text: My work is close to Soho, oddly

parts.note: go means work or function, as a machine does

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of the word Soho

explanation.surface: Someone's place of work is near Soho, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is the exclamation of surprise. Soho is a central London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, interchangeable in 'My, what a sight!'

clue.text: Try cutting furthest edges of grass — with these?

definitions.text: Try cutting furthest edges of grass — with these?

indicators.note: cutting into means one piece goes between the letters of the other
furthest points to the very end of the phrase, whose closing letters are the double S of grass

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it

explanation.surface: Try trimming the very edges of the lawn with these.
explanation.definitionFit: Large two-bladed cutters are the gardener's tool for trimming the margins of a lawn.

clue.text: Definitely packing collection of books ordered

indicators.note: packing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: indeed means definitely
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of biblical books

explanation.surface: Someone definitely packed the box of books they ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: To indent for goods is to place an official requisition for them.

clue.text: Oscar Wilde's best mate?

parts.note: the title of a Wilde comedy, read as describing the perfect marriage partner

explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's 1895 comedy has this title, and a perfect spouse is the finest partner one could wed.
